messages.text:
For the current baseline tracker, can you give me a table:

- Feature size (pixel/ strixel/ strip)
- Resulting estimated resolution(s)
- Number of channels (Barrel/EC)
I’ll check the current tracker baseline and its readout assumptions, then put the feature sizes, estimated resolutions and barrel/endcap channel counts into one table.
The baseline changed after PR #97: main now uses the balanced pixel layout selected on 29 October. I’ll use its updated pixel counts; the strixel and long-strip specifications are unchanged.

For the **current balanced baseline, selected 29 October**, the nominal counts are below. **EC includes both endcaps.** Resolutions are ideal binary hit estimates in local coordinates.

| Sensor type | Feature size | Estimated resolution(s) | Barrel channels | EC channels |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| [Pixel](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/b4928ac87a223dc4a749e8d8a05dc3cc4a78558d/docs/publication/tracker-baseline-2026-10-29/chapters/pixel-detector.tex) | 50 × 50 µm² | 14.4 × 14.4 µm² | 1,043,558,400 | 862,617,600 |
| [Strixel](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/b4928ac87a223dc4a749e8d8a05dc3cc4a78558d/docs/design/DES-007-short-strip-modules.md) | 75 µm × 0.5 mm | 21.7 × 144 µm² | 990,904,320 | 530,841,600 |
| [Long strip](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/b4928ac87a223dc4a749e8d8a05dc3cc4a78558d/docs/design/DES-008-long-strip-modules.md) | 80 µm pitch; 96 mm length | 23.1 µm per face; stereo pair: 16.3 µm across, 0.817 mm along strips | 16,761,600 | 8,985,600 |
| **Total** | | | **2,051,224,320** | **1,402,444,800** |

That is **3,453,669,120 channels overall**. Counts use the [current baseline inventory](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/b4928ac87a223dc4a749e8d8a05dc3cc4a78558d/docs/publication/tracker-baseline-2026-10-29/data/balanced-baseline.json): 153,600 channels per pixel chip, 122,880 per strixel sensor and 1,200 per strip face. Both strip faces are counted.

The estimates use σ = pitch/√12. The strip-pair result assumes **40 mrad relative stereo**, independent face errors and transport to a common plane; actual sensor response and alignment require further modelling.
